mainTopic: The מצורע's oil and the rules for when a עבודה must be done with the right hand
overview: This amud deals with the purification of a מצורע and then with the question of when a עבודה must be done with the right hand. First the גמרא explains why the תורה names the thumb and toe for the oil: one mention allows the sides (צדדין), and the other rules out the 'sides of the sides' (צידי צדדין). It then shows that both 'on the blood of the אשם' and 'on the place of the blood of the אשם' are needed. The oil goes on that spot even if the blood was wiped off, and blood that is still there is not a חציצה. רבא says the word 'right' for the oil is extra, so it teaches three גזירות שוות: right hand for קמיצה, right foot for חליצה, and right ear for רציעה. The extra 'left' teaches that the כהן's right hand is invalid for holding the oil. The rest of the repeated words come with a פרשה that is repeated for its one new detail. Then ריש לקיש teaches that 'finger' and 'כהונה' mean the right hand. רבא explains that either word is enough. After אביי's challenge, the גמרא limits this to an act that holds back כפרה. For רבי שמעון, 'finger' works alone but 'כהונה' needs 'finger', and the mention of a כהן teaches that he must serve in his priestly state.

steps.title: Finishing the question: the תורה already said 'on the blood of the guilt offering'
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a question that started earlier. Why does the תורה list the thumb and toe for the oil, if it already says the oil goes 'on the blood of the אשם'?
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, it is written: 'On the blood of the guilt offering'!
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a question that began before this section. The גמרא asks why the פסוק needs to name the thumb and toe for the oil when it already says the oil goes on the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of the אשם was already placed on the right ear, thumb and big toe. So 'on the blood' already tells us where the oil goes, and naming the body parts again looks extra. The גמרא is about to explain what that extra wording teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood of the guilt offering brought by a מצורע. It is put on his right ear, thumb and big toe.
'After all, it is written.' Points to a פסוק that seems to make another פסוק unnecessary.

phrases.english: After all, it is written: "On the blood of the guilt offering"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:17. Some versions leave out these words in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question begun before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra words in the פסוק naming the thumb and toe for the oil (for both the rich and the poor מצורע).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the oil goes 'on the blood', and the blood is already on the thumb and toe, then naming the thumb and toe again seems unnecessary.

steps.title: One mention allows the sides, the other rules out the 'sides of the sides'
steps.stepSummary: The two extra mentions of the thumb and toe teach two limits. One allows putting the oil on the sides. The other forbids the far sides, the underside.
steps.simpleTranslation: One mention is to make the sides valid, and one mention is to make the 'sides of the sides' invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the extra wording is not wasted. Each of the two mentions (rich מצורע and poor מצורע) teaches a separate rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One mention teaches that the oil may go on the sides of the thumb and toe, not only on the nail side. The other mention sets a limit: the 'sides of the sides', meaning the underside, are invalid. Together they mark exactly how far the valid area goes.

keyTerms.meaning: To make valid or acceptable.
To make invalid or disqualify.
The sides of the thumb or toe.
'Sides of the sides', the far underside of the thumb or toe.

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines in practice where the כהן may put the oil on the מצורע's thumb and toe.

phrases.english: One is to make the sides valid,
phrases.notes: 'One' means the mention in the section about the rich מצורע.

phrases.english: and one is to make the sides of the sides invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד לְהַכְשִׁיר צְדָדִין, וְחַד לִפְסוֹל צִידֵּי צְדָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives each seemingly extra phrase its own teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming the thumb and toe again seemed to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: One mention allows the sides, and the other rules out the sides of the sides.

steps.title: Why two different phrases: 'on the blood' and 'on the place of the blood'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה says 'on the blood of the אשם' for the rich מצורע but 'on the place of the blood of the אשם' for the poor one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On the blood of the guilt offering' and 'on the place of the blood of the guilt offering': what does each come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the two different wordings. It is setting up an explanation of why both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים describe the same act with slightly different words. The גמרא wants to know what each wording adds, since the תורה does not use words for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Place or location. Here, the spot where the blood was put.
'What do they come for?' What does each phrase teach?

phrases.english: "On the blood of the guilt offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:17, about the rich מצורע.

phrases.english: and "On the place of the blood of the guilt offering":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:28, about the poor מצורע. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: what do they come for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the body-part wording, the גמרא turns to the difference between the two phrases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the two wordings, 'on the blood' and 'on the place of the blood', teaches.

steps.title: Without 'on the place', we would require the blood to still be there
steps.stepSummary: Both phrases are needed. If the תורה said only 'on the blood', we would think the oil is placed only when the blood is still there, not after it was wiped off.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are needed. If the תורה had written only 'on the blood of the guilt offering', I would think: if the blood is there, yes; if it was wiped off, no. So the תורה wrote 'on the place'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a צריכותא, showing why each phrase is needed. This is the first half: why we need 'on the place'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'On the blood' alone sounds like the oil must go right on top of the blood. Then if the blood had been wiped away, we might say the oil cannot be placed. 'On the place' teaches that the location is what matters, not whether the blood is still there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They are needed.' Opens a צריכותא, an explanation of why each source is necessary.
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ as the One who gave the תורה.
'I would have said', the mistaken idea we would have had without this פסוק.
'It is there.' The blood is still on the thumb or toe.
'It was wiped off.' The blood is no longer there.

phrases.english: These are necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written "on the blood of the guilt offering,"
I would have said:
if it is there, yes,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the blood still on the thumb or toe.

phrases.english: if it was wiped off, no.
So the Merciful One wrote "on the place."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'On the place' teaches that the oil is placed even if the blood was wiped away.

steps.title: Without 'on the blood', we would think the blood is a barrier
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה said only 'on the place', we would think the oil may go there only after the blood was wiped off, because blood still there would block the oil. So the תורה also says 'on the blood'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only 'on the place', I would think: only if the blood was wiped off; but if it is still there, I would say it is a barrier. So it teaches us 'on the blood of the guilt offering'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the צריכותא, explaining why we also need 'on the blood'. With both halves, each phrase now has its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'On the place' alone might suggest the oil must touch the skin itself. Then blood still on the thumb or toe would be a חציצה blocking the oil. 'On the blood' teaches that putting oil on top of the blood is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically, only in that exact case.
A barrier that blocks direct contact and can make a מצוה act invalid.
'It teaches us', introducing what the source comes to tell us.

steps.whatToRemember: Both wordings are needed. 'On the place' means the oil is placed even after the blood was wiped off. 'On the blood' means blood still there is not a חציצה. Either way, the oil goes on that spot.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written "on the place,"
I would have said: only if it was wiped off,
but if it is there, I would say it is a barrier,
phrases.notes: The blood would block the oil from touching the skin.

phrases.english: so it teaches us "on the blood of the guilt offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'On the blood' teaches that blood still on the thumb or toe is not a חציצה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both phrases are needed. The oil goes on the spot whether the blood was wiped off or is still there.

steps.title: Why repeat 'right' for the oil?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: the oil goes where the blood went, and the blood is already on the right side, so why does the תורה say 'right' again for the oil of the rich and the poor מצורע?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The תורה says the oil goes 'on the blood of the אשם' and 'on the place of the blood of the אשם.' It also says the blood goes on the right thumb and the right big toe. So why does it say 'right' again for the oil, both for the rich מצורע and for the poor one?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a challenge. The word 'right' in the oil verses seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4-5 showed that the oil is put on the same spot as the blood. The blood verses already say that spot is on the right side. So the oil must go on the right side anyway, and saying 'right' again for the oil, twice (rich and poor), looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: the place (the spot where the blood was put)
right (the right side)
the thumb or the big toe
Why do I need it? (this seems extra)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since it is written "on the blood of the guilt offering"
and "on the place of the blood of the guilt offering,"
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; the corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: and "right" is written about the blood:
"on the thumb of his right hand
and on the big toe of his right foot,"
and they are written again about the oil
of the rich and the poor leper,
why do I need them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the result of steps 4-5 (oil goes on the place of the blood) to show that 'right' in the oil verses seems extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'right' in the oil verses of the rich and poor מצורע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The oil goes on the blood's place, and the blood is already on the right side, so 'right' for the oil teaches nothing new.

steps.title: 'Hand' teaches the right hand for קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the extra words are used for a גזירה שוה. 'Hand' here teaches about 'hand' in קמיצה: it must be done with the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The word 'hand' here is linked to the word 'hand' used for קמיצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer: the extra 'right hand' is not needed for the מצורע, so it teaches about a different מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the oil goes on the right side anyway, the word 'right' is free. Through a גזירה שוה it moves over to another place where the תורה says 'hand': taking the handful (קמיצה) from a מנחה. So קמיצה must also be done with the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (bringing a new explanation)
a link between two places that use the same word, so a law moves from one to the other
taking a handful of flour from a מנחה offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where we learn that קמיצה, a central act of the מנחות this מסכת deals with, must be done with the right hand.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
"Hand" here and "hand" there, for the taking of the handful.
phrases.notes: The 'right hand' of the מצורע teaches that the handful from a מנחה is also taken with the right hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by giving the extra 'right' a job outside the laws of the מצורע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirects the extra verse to teach a גזירה שוה for a different מצוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'right' for the oil seems to teach nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that קמיצה is done with the right hand.

steps.title: 'Foot' teaches חליצה, 'ear' teaches רציעה
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: 'foot' teaches that חליצה is done on the right foot, and 'ear' teaches that רציעה is done on the right ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Foot' here is linked to 'foot' in חליצה. 'Ear' here is linked to 'ear' in רציעה, the piercing of the slave's ear.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies the same idea to the foot and the ear: each extra word teaches 'right' for another מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like 'hand', the words 'right foot' and 'right ear' in the oil verses are not needed for the מצורע. 'Foot' teaches that in חליצה the shoe is taken off the right foot. 'Ear' teaches that a Hebrew slave's right ear is the one pierced.

keyTerms.meaning: the act of taking off the shoe of a man who does not marry his brother's widow
piercing the ear of a Hebrew slave who wants to stay with his master
ear

steps.whatToRemember: Because the oil goes on the place of the blood, the word 'right' in the oil verses is extra. רבא uses it for three גזירות שוות: right hand for קמיצה, right foot for חליצה, right ear for רציעה.

phrases.english: "Foot" here and "foot" there, for the removal of the shoe.
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9

phrases.english: "Ear" here and "ear" there, for the piercing.
phrases.notes: שמות 21:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's answer from step 7, using the same method for the foot and the ear.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same method as step 7: the extra word teaches a גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Right foot' and 'right ear' for the oil seem to teach nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They teach that חליצה is on the right foot and רציעה is on the right ear.

steps.title: Why repeat 'left' for the poor מצורע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה mentions the left hand again in the פרשה of the poor מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'left' in the פרשה of the poor מצורע: what does it come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with רבא's question style and now asks about another extra word: 'left' in the poor מצורע's פרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rich מצורע's פרשה already says the oil is poured into the כהן's left hand. So when the poor מצורע's פרשה says 'left' again, it looks extra. The גמרא wants to know what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: left (hand)
for what does it come? What does it teach?
poor person (here, a poor מצורע who brings a cheaper קרבן)

phrases.english: The word 'left' (of the poor person)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, but either way he means the 'left' in the poor מצורע's פרשה.

phrases.english: for what does it come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of extra-word question as רבא's, now about 'left'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repeated word 'left' in the poor מצורע's פרשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It was already said for the rich מצורע, so repeating it seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: Extra 'left' rules out the כהן's right hand
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי: the extra 'left' teaches that the כהן's right hand is not valid here, so we don't make a קל וחומר to allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: It comes to disqualify the כהן's right hand for the מצורע. So you should not say: In other places, where the left hand is not allowed, the right hand is allowed. So here, where even the left hand is allowed, surely the right hand is allowed too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא answers that the extra 'left' teaches that the oil may not be poured into the כהן's right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually only the right hand counts in עבודה. Since the left hand works here, one might reason by קל וחומר that the right hand works even better. The repeated 'left' blocks that reasoning: here only the left is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: to disqualify, to make invalid
a person with צרעת who brings קרבנות to become טהור
was included, is allowed
isn't it logical? (a קל וחומר formula)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'left' here is the כהן's own left hand, which holds the oil like a cup. It is not the right thumb or ear of the מצורע.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
to disqualify the right hand of the priest for a leper,
phrases.notes: The oil is poured into the כהן's palm. This teaches that pouring it into his right palm doesn't work.

phrases.english: so that you should not say:
If in a place where the left is not included
the right is included,
then in a place where the left is included,
isn't it logical that the right is included?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra word blocks a קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since even the left hand works for the מצורע, the right hand should surely work too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the כהן's left hand is valid for holding the מצורע's oil; the right hand is invalid.

steps.title: What about the other repeated words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the other repeated 'left', and 'right hand and foot', in the poor מצורע's פרשה teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other 'left' (and the 'right hand and foot' of the poor person): what do they come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: Only one extra 'left' has been explained. The גמרא now asks about the rest of the repeated words in the poor מצורע's פרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of the repeated words have already been given a job: the extra 'right' words teach the גזירות שוות (steps 7-8), and one extra 'left' rules out the right hand (step 10). But the poor מצורע's פרשה still has more repeated words, another 'left' and 'right hand and foot', that have not been explained. The גמרא asks what they are for.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other one
hand (thumb) and foot (big toe)
right

phrases.english: And the other 'left'
(and the right hand and foot of the poor person),
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: for what does it come?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ ״שְׂמָאלִית״ (וְיָד וָרֶגֶל יְמָנִית דְּעָנִי), לְמַאי אֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows step 10 by asking about the extra words that are still left.
steps.kashyaTarget: The remaining repeated words in the poor מצורע's פרשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every extra word must teach something, these leftover words still need a purpose.

steps.title: A repeated פרשה is only for its new detail
steps.stepSummary: Answer: following the school of רבי ישמעאל, a פרשה is sometimes repeated just for its one new detail, so the other repeated words need not teach anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: any פרשה that was said and then said again was repeated only for the sake of something new in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the leftover words don't need their own lesson. The whole poor מצורע's פרשה is repeated because of the new detail in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor מצורע's פרשה repeats the rich one's because something is new: the cheaper קרבנות. Once the תורה repeats a whole פרשה for that, the other words come along with it. We don't learn extra rules from each of them.

keyTerms.meaning: a section of the תורה
was said and then repeated
a new detail introduced in it

steps.whatToRemember: Not every repeated word in the תורה must teach a new rule. When a whole פרשה is repeated for one new point, the rest of it is just there for that point.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל puts a limit on learning from extra words, and it is used in many places.

phrases.english: For that which the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Any passage that was stated and repeated,
was repeated only
for the sake of a matter that was newly introduced in it.
phrases.notes: Here the new matter is the poor מצורע's cheaper קרבנות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 and closes the discussion of extra words in the מצורע's פרשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule of how the תורה is written
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every leftover repeated word must teach its own rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leftover words are part of a פרשה repeated for its new detail, so they teach nothing extra.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: 'finger' and 'כהונה' mean the right hand
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes ריש לקיש: wherever the תורה says 'finger' and 'כהונה', the act is done only with the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: Any place where 'finger' and 'כהונה' are said, it means only the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: a general rule for knowing when an עבודה must be done with the right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש gives two clues in a פסוק that mean right hand: the word 'finger' and the word 'כהן'. The wording 'finger and כהונה' is unclear: are both needed, or is one enough? The next steps deal with that.

keyTerms.meaning: finger
priesthood; a פסוק that mentions the כהן
right hand

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said,
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Any place where finger and priesthood are stated,
it is only the right hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרָה אֶצְבַּע וּכְהוּנָּה, אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא יָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic: general clues for when the right hand is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a פסוק mentions 'finger' and 'כהונה', the עבודה must be done with the right hand.

steps.title: First reading: both words are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first thinks ריש לקיש means both 'finger' and 'כהונה' must be in the פסוק, as with the חטאת's blood, which is learned from the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: We first thought: we need both finger and כהונה. As it is written: 'And the כהן shall take of the blood of the חטאת with his finger.' And this is learned from מצורע, where it is written: 'And the כהן shall dip his right finger.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a first understanding of ריש לקיש, and it is about to challenge it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, a פסוק needs both words, like the חטאת פסוק that says 'כהן' and 'finger'. That 'finger' means right is learned from the מצורע's פסוק, which openly says 'right finger'. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: it enters our mind; our first thought
we require
sin offering
and he learns it (from another פסוק)

phrases.english: It entered our mind,
we require finger and priesthood together,
as it is written:
"And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering with his finger",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:25

phrases.english: and it is learned from the leper, where it is written:
"And the priest shall dip his right finger".
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:16

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין, אֶצְבַּע וּכְהוּנָּה בָּעֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first reading of ריש לקיש's words from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does ריש לקיש require both 'finger' and 'כהונה' in the same פסוק?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first thought is yes, both are needed. Step 15 challenges this.

steps.title: קמיצה says only כהונה, yet the left hand is invalid
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: the פסוק of קמיצה mentions only כהונה, yet the משנה rules that קמיצה with the left hand is invalid, so 'כהונה' alone must be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at קמיצה: only כהונה is written there, and we learned in a משנה: if he took the handful with his left hand, it is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first reading. Here is a case with only 'כהונה' and no 'finger', and still the right hand is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both words were needed, קמיצה would not need the right hand, since its פסוק says only 'כהן'. But the משנה rules that קמיצה with the left hand is invalid. So the reading that both words are required looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: the כהן taking a handful from a מנחה
but look at
invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with step 7. There רבא learned the right hand for קמיצה from a גזירה שוה. Here the question is only whether ריש לקיש's rule fits קמיצה.

phrases.english: But there is the removal of a handful,
in which only priesthood is written,
and we learned: If he removed the handful with the left, it is invalid!
phrases.notes: This is the משנה earlier in this מסכת, on דף ו.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי קְמִיצָה דְּלָא כְּתִיבָא בָּהּ אֶלָּא כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first reading given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that ריש לקיש needs both 'finger' and 'כהונה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קמיצה has only 'כהונה', yet the left hand is invalid, so 'כהונה' alone must require the right hand.

steps.title: רבא: either finger or priesthood is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains ריש לקיש's rule: the right hand is needed if the פסוק says either 'finger' or 'כהונה'. Both words are not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is enough if the פסוק says either 'finger' or 'כהונה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the problem from קמיצה by changing how we read ריש לקיש. The right hand is required when either word appears in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 first thought both 'finger' and 'כהונה' had to appear together. Step 15 showed that קמיצה needs the right hand even though only 'כהונה' is written. So רבא says each word works alone, and that fits the קמיצה case.

keyTerms.meaning: Finger. When this word appears, the act is done with the right hand.
Priesthood. The פסוק mentions a כהן doing the act.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Either "finger" or "priesthood".
phrases.notes: He means either word by itself is enough to require the right hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אוֹ אֶצְבַּע אוֹ כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by reading ריש לקיש's rule as 'either/or'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both 'finger' and 'כהונה' must appear in the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either word alone requires the right hand.

steps.title: אביי's challenge from carrying limbs to the ramp
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to carrying the limbs to the ramp. The פסוק mentions a כהן, yet a משנה says the right leg is carried in the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Look at carrying the limbs to the ramp. כהונה is written about it, since the פסוק says 'And the כהן shall bring all of it to the altar', and the Master said this refers to carrying the limbs to the ramp. Yet we learned in a משנה: the right leg is held in the left hand, with its skin side facing outward.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's 'either/or' rule. He brings a case where כהונה is written, but the left hand is clearly allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'כהונה' alone required the right hand, every part of carrying the limbs would need the right hand. The משנה has the כהן hold a limb in his left hand. So 'כהונה' alone seems not to be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the limbs of the קרבן toward the altar.
The ramp that leads up to the altar.
The side of the limb covered with skin.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But there is the carrying of the limbs to the ramp,
about which priesthood is written,
as it is written: "And the priest shall bring
all of it to the altar",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:13

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר מָר: זוֹ הוֹלָכַת אֵבָרִים לַכֶּבֶשׁ,
phrases.english: and the Master said: this is the carrying of the limbs to the ramp,
and we learned: the right leg is held in the left hand,
and its skin side faces outward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הֲרֵי הוֹלָכַת אֵבָרִים לַכֶּבֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's 'either/or' rule from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that 'כהונה' alone requires the right hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying the limbs has כהונה in its פסוק, yet the משנה allows the left hand. So the rule does not hold.

steps.title: The rule applies only to acts that hold back atonement
steps.stepSummary: The 'either finger or כהונה' rule applies only to an act that holds back כפרה. Carrying the limbs is not such an act.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we say 'either finger or כהונה', that is only for something that holds back כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by limiting his rule. It covers only acts that the כפרה depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying the limbs to the ramp does not stop the כפרה if it is missing. So even though כהונה is written there, the left hand is allowed. The rule now has a new condition: the act must be מעכב כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: An act without which the קרבן does not bring atonement.
Atonement that the קרבן brings.

phrases.english: When we say "either finger or priesthood",
it is about a matter that holds back atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָמְרִינַן אוֹ אֶצְבַּע אוֹ כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's קשיא by narrowing רבא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any act whose פסוק mentions כהונה needs the right hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only acts that hold back כפרה need the right hand when 'finger' or 'כהונה' is written.

steps.title: Challenge from receiving the blood
steps.stepSummary: Receiving the blood holds back כפרה, and its פסוק mentions כהונה. Yet רבי שמעון allows receiving it with the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But receiving the blood is something that holds back כפרה, and כהונה is written about it, since the פסוק says 'And the sons of אהרן, the כהנים, shall bring the blood', and this means receiving the blood. Yet we learned in a משנה: if he received it with the left hand, it is invalid, and רבי שמעון rules it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the narrowed rule from step 18. Receiving the blood meets both conditions, yet רבי שמעון allows the left hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Receiving the blood holds back כפרה, and כהונה is in its פסוק. By the rule of step 18 it should need the right hand. The first opinion in the משנה fits that, but רבי שמעון says the left hand is valid, so the rule does not fit his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving the קרבן's blood in a holy vessel.
Made it invalid.
Rules it valid.

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not with the first opinion, which agrees the left hand is invalid. The challenge comes only from רבי שמעון, who allows the left hand.

phrases.english: But there is receiving the blood, which is a matter that holds back atonement,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and priesthood is written about it,
as it is written: "And the sons of Aharon
the priests, shall bring the blood",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:5

phrases.english: this means receiving the blood,
and we learned: if he received it with the left hand, it is invalid,
and Rabbi Shimon rules it valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי קַבָּלָה דְּדָבָר הַמְעַכֵּב כַּפָּרָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrowed rule given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that 'finger' or 'כהונה' requires the right hand for acts that hold back כפרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Receiving the blood holds back כפרה and has כהונה written, yet רבי שמעון allows the left hand.

steps.title: The left-hand ruling follows רבי שמעון, who needs both words
steps.stepSummary: The question came from רבי שמעון's view. רבי שמעון needs both 'finger' and 'כהונה' before the right hand is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are asking from רבי שמעון's view? רבי שמעון needs both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 19. The case of receiving blood with the left hand follows רבי שמעון, and he works by a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule from Step 16 was that one word, 'finger' or 'כהונה', is enough to require the right hand. רבי שמעון disagrees and requires both words in the פסוק. The receiving-blood פסוק mentions only כהונה, so for him the left hand is valid. That means there is no question on רבא, because רבא is not following רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Two, both (here: both 'finger' and 'כהונה')
Requires, needs
You are saying

phrases.english: You are asking from רבי שמעון's view?
רבי שמעון requires both.
phrases.notes: Both words have to be in the פסוק: 'finger' and 'כהונה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19 by saying it follows a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the source to a different opinion (רבי שמעון) that has a stricter rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The receiving-blood ruling seemed to go against רבא's 'either word' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: That ruling follows רבי שמעון, who requires both words. רבא's rule stays in place for everyone else.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that for רבי שמעון one word is enough
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון saying that 'hand' or 'finger' alone always means the right hand. So he does not seem to need both words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון really need both? A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, anywhere the תורה says 'hand', it means only the right hand. Anywhere it says 'finger', it means only the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 20. It brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון seems to need only one word to require the right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said רבי שמעון needs both 'finger' and 'כהונה'. In this ברייתא he says the word 'finger' by itself is enough to mean the right hand. That seems to contradict the claim that he needs two words.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really require? (opens a challenge)
Anywhere it is said (a general rule)
Hand
Finger
The right hand

phrases.english: And does רבי שמעון really require both?
But a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרָה ״יָד״ – אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא יָמִין,
phrases.english: Any place where 'hand' is said, it means only the right,
and 'finger' means only the right!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי בָּעֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן תַּרְתֵּי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim of Step 20 about רבי שמעון's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 20's claim that רבי שמעון requires both words.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's own words show that 'finger' alone means the right hand, so he does not need two words.

steps.title: 'Finger' works alone, but 'כהונה' needs 'finger'
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון, 'finger' alone is enough. 'כהונה' alone is not enough unless 'finger' is also there.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Finger' does not need כהונה. כהונה does need 'finger'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It makes clear what 'needs both' means for רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'both' rule only goes one way. The word 'finger' by itself requires the right hand, just as the ברייתא says. The word 'כהונה' only counts when 'finger' is also in the פסוק. So the receiving-blood פסוק, which mentions only כהונה, does not require the right hand. That fits רבי שמעון's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not require
Priesthood (a mention of the כהן in the פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'רבי שמעון needs both' as meaning neither word works alone. 'Finger' does work alone. Only 'כהונה' needs help.

phrases.english: 'Finger' does not require כהונה,
but כהונה requires 'finger'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by making the 'both' rule of Step 20 more exact.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Makes the rule more precise: the requirement works in one direction only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Needs both' seemed to mean that 'finger' alone is not enough, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Finger' alone is enough. 'כהונה' alone is not. So receiving blood, where only כהונה is mentioned, can be done with the left hand.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון: 'finger' alone requires the right hand, but 'כהונה' alone does not.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק mention a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: If כהונה alone does not require the right hand, why does the פסוק mention a כהן at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why do I need the word 'כהן'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If the mention of a כהן does not teach 'right hand' for רבי שמעון, what does it teach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה should teach something. For רבי שמעון the mention of a כהן in this פסוק does not teach the right-hand rule. So the גמרא asks why it is there.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks what a word is for)
A כהן, a priest

phrases.english: But then why do I need 'כהן'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 22: if כהונה does not teach 'right hand', its purpose has to be found.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra mention of a כהן in the פסוק, according to רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the word does not teach the right-hand rule, it seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: It teaches that the כהן must be in his priestly state
steps.stepSummary: The mention of a כהן teaches that he must do the service in his priestly state, wearing the priestly clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches: in his priestly state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 23. The word 'כהן' teaches a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra mention of a כהן is not wasted. It teaches that the כהן must serve while he is in his priestly state, wearing the בגדי כהונה. So it has a purpose without teaching the right-hand rule.

keyTerms.meaning: In his priestly state (wearing the priestly clothes)
The priestly clothes

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the mention of a כהן in this פסוק teaches 'in his priestly state', not 'right hand'.

phrases.english: In his priestly state.
phrases.notes: He has to be dressed as a כהן, wearing the priestly clothes, while he does it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 by giving a different purpose for the word 'כהן'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the right-hand teaching, the word 'כהן' seemed to have no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'כהן' teaches that the service must be done while the כהן is in his priestly state.
